_readme: Validation set for the two §5.4 judge checks that had no ground truth (PLAN.md D30): UNSUPPORTED and CAUSAL.
One sentence per unit and kind, inserted at the end of the traditional primary's Explanation by
scripts/build_judge_probes.py, which writes stimuli/judge_probes/ and checks that nothing else changed.
kinds: `unsupported` asserts a quantity or fact the unit never states and that cannot be derived from it;
`causal` asserts a causal relation the material does not license; `background` is a hard negative - standard
domain knowledge a lesson may legitimately state, which the judge must NOT flag. These texts are judge inputs
only: they are never read by a simulated learner and never predicted by the encoding model.

be_001.unsupported: The sales team already holds firm orders for 4,200 of those units, so only the remainder is at risk.
be_001.causal: A lower break-even point causes a company's sales to grow.
be_001.background: Fixed costs are the costs that do not change with the number of units sold within the range being considered, such as rent or an annual licence.

be_002.unsupported: The pitch is busiest at lunchtime, when the truck serves about 60 meals an hour.
be_002.causal: Selling above the break-even quantity causes the ingredient cost of each meal to fall.
be_002.background: Break-even analysis assumes that the selling price and the variable cost of a unit stay the same across the range of sales considered.

cac_001.unsupported: About a fifth of these customers arrived through a referral scheme that costs the company nothing.
cac_001.causal: A shorter payback period causes customers to stay loyal for longer.
cac_001.background: The acquisition cost of a customer is the sales and marketing spending of a period divided by the number of customers it brought in.

cac_002.unsupported: The company also earns EUR 20 a month from each customer through a partner commission that is not part of the margin above.
cac_002.causal: Spending more on marketing causes the gross margin on subscriptions to improve.
cac_002.background: Payback is counted in months of gross margin, so a business with a thin margin recovers its acquisition cost more slowly.

cm_001.unsupported: Roughly 30% of the subscribers pay a year in advance, which brings the cash in sooner.
cm_001.causal: A higher contribution margin ratio causes subscribers to renew.
cm_001.background: The contribution margin ratio is the share of each euro of revenue that is left once the variable costs of serving it have been paid.

cm_002.unsupported: The company's largest client accounts for EUR 90,000 of that revenue on its own.
cm_002.causal: Winning more contracts causes the labour cost of each contract to fall.
cm_002.background: Break-even is expressed in revenue rather than in units when a business sells work of differing sizes, where a count of units would mean little.

dol_001.unsupported: The manufacturer expects its volume to grow by 6% next year.
dol_001.causal: A high degree of operating leverage causes a firm's sales to become volatile.
dol_001.background: Operating leverage measures how strongly profit responds to a change in sales, not how profitable a firm is.

dol_002.unsupported: About 15% of those licences are renewed monthly rather than annually.
dol_002.causal: Higher fixed costs cause a software firm to sell more licences.
dol_002.background: A firm whose costs are mostly fixed sees its profit swing more sharply in both directions than a firm whose costs move with volume.

ltv_001.unsupported: Customers who stay beyond their first year spend about 20% more each month.
ltv_001.causal: A high lifetime value causes customers to cancel less often.
ltv_001.background: When the cancellation rate is steady, the average time a customer stays is the reciprocal of that rate.

ltv_002.unsupported: The company also charges a one-off joining fee of EUR 15.
ltv_002.causal: Improving the gross margin causes the monthly cancellation rate to fall.
ltv_002.background: A lifetime value computed before discounting overstates a customer whose margin arrives years from now.

mix_001.unsupported: Product B sells mainly in the last quarter of the year, when the shop takes about 40% of its revenue.
mix_001.causal: Selling more of product A causes the fixed costs to fall.
mix_001.background: A sales mix is only useful for as long as the proportions in which the products sell stay roughly stable.

mix_002.unsupported: The bakery throws away about 5% of its loaves unsold each day.
mix_002.causal: Baking more cakes causes the loaves to sell faster.
mix_002.background: With more than one product the break-even point is first found in bundles of the mix and then converted back into individual items.

mkp_001.unsupported: The retailer's competitors sell the same item for about EUR 95.
mkp_001.causal: Charging a higher price causes customers to value an item more.
mkp_001.background: Margin is a share of the selling price and markup is a share of the cost, so the two percentages are never equal for the same price.

mkp_002.unsupported: The boutique marks its jackets down by 20% in the January sale.
mkp_002.causal: A higher gross margin causes a boutique to sell more jackets.
mkp_002.background: Because margin is a share of the price, the cost is divided by one minus the margin rather than multiplied by one plus it.

mos_001.unsupported: Sales have fallen short of budget in three of the past five years.
mos_001.causal: A larger margin of safety causes budgeted sales to be achieved.
mos_001.background: The margin of safety shows how far sales can fall before a business stops covering its costs.

mos_002.unsupported: The hotel runs at about 70% occupancy across the year.
mos_002.causal: Reducing the break-even point causes guests to book earlier.
mos_002.background: Stating the cushion as a share of budgeted revenue keeps the measure comparable across businesses of different sizes.

npv_001.unsupported: The project would also release EUR 8,000 of working capital at the end of the second year.
npv_001.causal: A positive net present value causes a project to finish on schedule.
npv_001.background: The required return stands for what the same money could earn elsewhere at the same risk.

npv_002.unsupported: The machine could be resold for about EUR 12,000 at the end of the second year.
npv_002.causal: Discounting the savings causes the machine to last longer.
npv_002.background: A cash flow that arrives later is divided by a higher power of the same factor, one power for each year of waiting.

pbp_001.unsupported: The equipment is expected to need an overhaul costing EUR 6,000 in its third year.
pbp_001.causal: A shorter payback period causes equipment to break down less often.
pbp_001.background: Depreciation is an accounting allocation of a cost that has already been paid, not a payment made in the year it is charged.

pbp_002.unsupported: The hotel also expects the new kitchen to cut its energy bill by EUR 2,000 a year.
pbp_002.causal: Recovering an investment sooner causes the kitchen to generate more cash each year.
pbp_002.background: Payback ignores everything that happens once the investment has been recovered, including how long the asset goes on working.

pel_001.unsupported: Most of the customers who stopped buying now go to the shop next door.
pel_001.causal: Raising the price causes customers to value a latte more highly.
pel_001.background: Elasticity compares percentage changes, so its value does not depend on the units in which price and quantity are measured.

pel_002.unsupported: About 200 of the members who left had joined only the month before.
pel_002.causal: Elastic demand causes a gym to lose members.
pel_002.background: Demand is called elastic when the percentage fall in quantity is larger than the percentage rise in price.

roi_001.unsupported: The project ran for four years, so that gain is spread across four annual periods.
roi_001.causal: A higher return on investment causes a project to need less capital.
roi_001.background: Return on investment relates the gain to the amount invested and says nothing about how long the money was tied up.

roi_002.unsupported: The equipment was financed with a loan carrying 4% interest.
roi_002.causal: Buying equipment causes a company's return on investment to rise.
roi_002.background: Because it ignores timing, return on investment cannot distinguish a gain earned in one year from the same gain earned over ten.

spo_001.unsupported: The customer has indicated that it would place a similar order every year.
spo_001.causal: Winning export orders causes a manufacturer's domestic sales to grow.
spo_001.background: A cost is relevant to a decision only if it changes as a result of that decision.

spo_002.unsupported: The licence can be reused on two later jobs at no extra cost.
spo_002.causal: Taking on customisation work causes a software firm's overhead to fall.
spo_002.background: Capacity that is already paid for and would otherwise sit idle carries no incremental cost, which is why those hours do not enter the comparison.

tp_001.unsupported: The company expects to sell about 9,000 units next year before any special effort.
tp_001.causal: Paying a higher rate of tax causes a company to sell more units.
tp_001.background: A profit target set after tax has to be grossed up, because tax is charged on the profit earned before it.

tp_002.unsupported: The studio's rooms allow it to run at most 700 courses a year.
tp_002.causal: Selling more courses causes the rate of tax to rise.
tp_002.background: Dividing the after-tax target by one minus the tax rate turns it into the pre-tax profit that has to be earned.

wac_001.unsupported: The firm plans to repay EUR 50 million of that debt next year.
wac_001.causal: Issuing debt causes shareholders to require a lower return.
wac_001.background: Interest is deductible against tax, which is why the cost of debt is counted after tax.

wac_002.unsupported: The firm's debt matures in three years.
wac_002.causal: A lower weighted average cost of capital causes a firm's projects to succeed.
wac_002.background: The weights are the shares of each source in the firm's total financing, not the amounts themselves.
